title: Calculation Sheet: Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Unpaid Installment Late Charge
content:
**Schedule of Servicing Fees — calculation sheet, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

## The unpaid installment portion

The unpaid installment portion is the unpaid portion, as of the assessment date, of the installment the contract's next due date shows: payments reach the oldest installment first, so every later past-due installment is wholly unpaid, and the unpaid installment portion is the contract's past-due amount less one monthly payment for each whole monthly payment contained in the past-due amount less one cent, rounded to the cent.

## The charge

The unpaid installment late charge is the product's late-charge percentage of the unpaid installment (as the product's late charge schedule gives it for the contract's tier) applied to the unpaid installment portion, rounded to the cent, and that figure is capped at the lower of the product's company maximum late charge and the state maximum late charge recorded on the contract. The percentage is one rate for the contract, applied once to the unpaid installment portion; the charge is booked to the cent and is never below zero.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Monthly payment 610.00 dollars, past-due amount 1,000.00 dollars, a hypothetical late-charge percentage of 6 percent, a company maximum of 30.00 dollars and a recorded state maximum of 20.00 dollars.

1. 1,000.00 less one cent is 999.99, which contains 1 whole monthly payment.
2. The unpaid installment portion is 1,000.00 less 610.00, which is 390.00 dollars.
3. 6 percent of 390.00 is 23.40 dollars.
4. The cap is the lower of 30.00 and 20.00, which is 20.00 dollars; 23.40 exceeds it, so the charge is 20.00 dollars.

A past-due amount of 300.00 dollars on the same contract (part of one installment unpaid) gives an unpaid portion of 300.00 dollars, since 299.99 contains no whole monthly payment.
